segments.english: §12. Behold, then, surely all your words are exaggerations and hyperboles, to alarm the fools and the madmen who love wonders and impossibilities, and you speak without knowledge. And all your words are without reason. And in deceit you refuse to know the LORD, as the prophet Jeremiah, peace be upon him, said in the name of the LORD: "Your dwelling is in the midst of deceit; through deceit they have refused to know Me, declares the LORD." And already one of the deceivers among you has said: "We know that the truth is with you." But what business is it of yours to reveal this matter and to publicize it to some of the students. It would be better for you to leave them in their error entirely, as the words of the wicked one among the four sons, who says: "What is this service to you? etc." And the proof that you daub whitewash: for in this letter of yours you published that the Rabbi, the author of Matzref ha-Emunah, is, God forbid, a heretic and a denier. And you called his book Mesharef ha-Emunah. And he, in his integrity, walks without turning aside from the words of the Zohar, and Mikdash Melekh, and Kisse Eliyahu, and the RaShB, and Yosher Levav, and Sefer ha-Berit, and Rabbi the Ari, and Rabbi Chayyim Vital in the book Etz Chayyim, and Nachalat Yosef, and their finest flour, to the right or to the left. As will be explained below, and first I will bring you several proofs. This Kabbalah is not a halakhah given to Moses at Sinai, for our Rabbis of blessed memory said in Eruvin: "Any baraita that is not taught in the house of Rabbi Oshaya, it is not a baraita, and you may not object from it, for it is corrupted." Thus, any baraita that did not enter the study-house of Rabbi Chiyya or of Rabbi Oshaya, not only is it not a halakhah given to Moses at Sinai. But one may not even raise an objection from it against an Amora. And in the Yerushalmi, Eruvin, chapter one, in the passage de-Lechayyim, it is written. And these are his words: "Acha said to him: So said Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish: any mishnah that did not enter the fellowship, one does not rely on it." Thus far. And see below, §42. And in an old notebook of the compositions of our forefathers I found written in the name of Rabbi Saadia Gaon, and these are his words: "The book Shiur Komah: no trustworthy transmission has come down concerning it, for it is not in the Mishnah and not in the Talmud. And there is no proof by which we can infer whether Rabbi Ishmael truly said it, or another said it and ascribed it to him, as many of the forged books are ascribed to some of the famous scholars." Thus far his words. (Translation by the Rabbi, the author: "The book Shiur Komah: we have no tradition concerning it from the sages of our faith, since it is neither in the Mishnah nor in the Talmud, and also there is no proof to be drawn from it whether Rabbi Ishmael truly said it, or others besides him said it and ascribed it to Rabbi Ishmael, as they ascribe many of the books that were made to some of the famous sages.")

tokens.note: The section number as the author gives it; the book's sections are numbered through the whole book, from §2 at 3:1 to §144 at 10:6.
The ש is not carried by an English 'that': 'surely all your words are ...'.
Literal 'cuttings'; גוזמא in the Talmud is the word for hyperbole, set beside הפלגות as a second word for exaggeration.
The object marker את; no English counterpart.
Construct chain: 'lovers of the wonders and the impossibilities'.
The negation ולא governs 'with knowledge'.
לא negates 'with reason'.
השכל: reason, understanding.
The object marker את; no English counterpart.
The Tetragrammaton as written. The pack splits it into ה and the apostrophe, which is punctuation.
ע"ה: 'peace be upon him', an honorific for a prophet.
שִׁבְתְּךָ in the verse is a noun ('your sitting, dwelling'); the verse has no verb: 'Your dwelling is in the midst of deceit'.
A perfect (מאנו), rendered 'have refused' as in the verse.
The Tetragrammaton as written, closing the verse's 'נאם ה''.
The word for deceivers shares the root of מרמה, 'deceit', in the verse above.
מה לכם: the idiom 'what is it to you', rendered as 'what business is it of yours'.
'matter', with 'this' in the next token.

ממש is placed after בטעותם but may belong with כדברי ('exactly as the words of the wicked one'). Question: read 'in their error, exactly as the words of the wicked one among the four sons' (proposed) rather than 'in their error entirely'. See readings.
The wicked son of the four sons of the Passover Haggadah.

Question: Exod 12:26, the verse the Haggadah's wicked son speaks, has עבודה for the Passover rite. The rulings fix 'worship' for עבודה of God or gods and 'serve' for a human master, and are silent on a rite. Proposed ruling: keep 'service' here with this note, and record 'worship' in readings.
Truncated quotation: וכו' is kept as 'etc.'.
טח: 'daubing' (plastering a wall). The pair טח תפל echoes Ezek 13:10 and 22:28, the false prophets who daub a wall with whitewash: speech that covers the flaw with a flimsy coat.
תפל: whitewash, untempered mortar (Ezek 13:10); the same word also means 'insipid, unsalted'.
בעל: 'the author of' (the Hebrew says בעל, so the English keeps it).
Matzref ha-Emunah: 'the refining of faith', from צרף, 'refine'. It is the title of the Rabbi's book.
ח"ו: God forbid.
Mesharef ha-Emunah: 'the burning of faith', from שרף, 'burn'. The interlocutor's name for the book, a pun on Matzref (3:12.88).
Mikdash Melekh: 'the sanctuary of the king'; a book title, transliterated.
Kisse Eliyahu: 'Elijah's throne'; the abbreviation כס"א is written out.
The acronym is kept as the author writes it; the work it names is not identified in this unit.
Yosher Levav: 'uprightness of heart'.
Sefer ha-Berit: 'the book of the covenant'.
The Ari: the name by which these texts call Isaac Luria.
מהרח"ו: Rabbi Chayyim Vital, the acronym written out.
Etz Chayyim: 'tree of life'.
Nachalat Yosef: 'the inheritance of Joseph'.
סולתם: 'their fine flour', that is, the best of them. With ימין ושמאל it completes לא סר: 'has not turned aside ... to the right or to the left' (Deut 17:11; Josh 1:7).
The ש opens a clause; the English makes 'This Kabbalah is not...' the main clause, after the full stop kept before it.
הקבלה: 'the Kabbalah', the lore, set against the halakhah given to Moses at Sinai.
הלכה למשה מסיני: 'a halakhah given to Moses at Sinai'.
Eruvin: the tractate, transliterated.
מתניתא: 'baraita', a tannaitic text outside the Mishnah.
בי: 'the house of', here the study-house of Rabbi Oshaya.
The subject pronoun 'it'; the English gives it once, before 'is not'.
דמשבשתא: 'that it is corrupted'.
The copula 'it is'.
בית מדרשו של: literally 'the house of his study of'; English 'the study-house of'.
לא מיבעיא: Aramaic, literally 'it is not needed to ask'; with אלא דאפילו it means 'not only ... but even'.
An Amora: a Talmudic sage of the generations after the tannaim.
קמא: 'the first', chapter one.
The Yerushalmi passage is named by its opening word. The Hebrew has no verb here, so 'it is written' supplies the main clause.
'de-Lechayyim': 'of life'; the passage is named by its first word.
חבורה: the study fellowship (chaburah).
ע"כ: the closing formula of the quotation, 'thus far'.
§42: the author's section number.
קונדריס: a notebook.
Judeo-Arabic kitāb, 'book'; translated from the Arabic as it stands.
Shiur Komah: 'measure of the stature', a mystical text on the measurements of the divine body.

Question: אמנתא is read as amāna(tan), 'trustworthy' (a reliable transmission). The author's Hebrew has מחכמי אמונתנו, 'the sages of our faith', which suggests amānatinā ('of our faith'). Proposed ruling: keep 'trustworthy' as the Arabic stands and give 'transmission of our faith' in readings and apparatus.
אר: evidently a scribal ר for ד, that is אד (idh), 'since, because'. Translated 'for'. Alternative: none that fits.
Judeo-Arabic nastadill, from istadalla, 'to infer, argue': 'we can infer'. The nun is the first-person plural prefix.
עלי׳ is עלי, ʿalā 'in, upon', with a geresh marking the alif maqsura (written yod); it is not 'him'. עלי׳ אלחקיקה = 'in truth'.
תנסב: passive (tunsab), 'are ascribed'.
Literally 'fabricated, invented' (iftaʿala); a book forged in the name of an authority.
עכ"ל: closing formula, 'thus far his words'.
קבלה: tradition; here the tradition about the book, in the author's own Hebrew.

העשויים: 'made'; the Arabic has 'forged'. The Hebrew order 'ascribe many of the books that were made to some of the famous sages' may also be read 'books made in the name of some of the sages'; see readings.
לקצת: 'to some', the sages to whom the books are ascribed.

grammar: Section label §12 (token 1). 'Behold, then, surely all your words are exaggerations and hyperboles': הפלגות and גיזומים (גוזמא) both name exaggeration; 'to alarm' (להבהיל) gives the purpose.
Jer 9:5 is quoted after כמאמר ... בשם ה'. שבתך is a noun, 'your dwelling'; מאנו is a perfect, 'have refused'.

שאתה טח תפל echoes Ezek 13:10 and 22:28 (daubing whitewash on a wall): 'you daub whitewash'. וקראת את ספרו משרף האמונה: קרא takes two objects, 'you called his book Mesharef ha-Emunah', a pun on Matzref ha-Emunah.

לא סר ... ימין ושמאל echoes Deut 17:11 and Josh 1:7: he has not turned aside, to the right or to the left, from the Zohar and the other works and their finest flour. לא מיבעיא ... אלא דאפילו is Aramaic 'not only ... but even'.

The Eruvin passage is Bavli Aramaic; the Yerushalmi passage is Yerushalmi Aramaic and has no verb in the Hebrew, so 'it is written' supplies the main clause. The Haggadah words are from Exod 12:26, given with וכו'.

Judeo-Arabic (Saadia): the geresh in עלי׳ and אלי׳ marks the alif maqsura (ʿalā 'in', ilā 'to'); אליה is ilayhi 'to him'. אר is a slip for אד (idh) 'since'. נסתדל is first person plural 'we infer'. פנסבה carries an object suffix: 'and ascribed it'; תנסב is passive 'are ascribed'. The author's Hebrew in parentheses is translated from the Hebrew.
segments.note: The Saadia passage is Judeo-Arabic and is translated from the Arabic as it stands. The author's own Hebrew translation, in parentheses, is translated from its own Hebrew and not copied from the Arabic; the differences are in apparatus. The owner's Q4 answer lists the Judeo-Arabic units for Sonnet (5:3, 7:24, 9:10, 2:13); 3:12 carries Judeo-Arabic but is not on that list. Flagged for the owner. The Yerushalmi passage has no verb in the Hebrew, so 'it is written' supplies the main clause.
apparatus: Base text from Wikisource; collation with the 1931 scan not yet made (open question 2).
Jer 9:5, quoted by the author: 'שבתך בתוך מרמה במרמה מאנו דעת אותי נאם ה''.
Exod 12:26 (the verse the wicked son speaks in the Haggadah): 'מה העבודה הזאת לכם'; the author gives it with וכו'.
Ezek 13:10 (also 22:28): 'וטחים אתו תפל', allusion in 'אתה טח תפל'.
Deut 17:11 (also Josh 1:7): 'לא תסור ... ימין ושמאל', allusion in 'לא סר ... ימין ושמאל'.
The Eruvin (Bavli) and Yerushalmi passages carry no folio or column in the author's text, and none is added.
וקראת (3:12.94): 'you called' (the pun on Matzref); alternative 'you read'.

Judeo-Arabic, translated from the Arabic as it stands. אר (3:12.235) is read as אד (idh) 'since'. אמנתא (3:12.234) is read amāna 'trustworthy'; alternative amānatinā 'of our faith', as the author's Hebrew has אמונתנו.

Arabic against the author's Hebrew: (1) 'no trustworthy transmission has come down concerning it' against 'we have no tradition concerning it from the sages of our faith' (the Hebrew adds 'from the sages'); (2) 'we can infer' against 'to be drawn from it'; (3) 'or another' against 'or others besides him'; (4) 'forged books ... to some famous scholars' against 'books made for some of the famous sages' (the Arabic has the forged books and says nothing of Rabbi Ishmael in that clause); (5) the Arabic has no 'also'.
context: The four sons of the Passover Haggadah: the wise, the wicked, the simple, and the one who does not know how to ask. The wicked son asks, 'What is this service to you?'

Shiur Komah ('measure of the stature') is a mystical text describing the measurements of the divine body, attributed to Rabbi Ishmael. The author and the Saadia passage both say that it is not in the Mishnah or the Talmud.
